narr: Low pressure crossed through the region on March 18th accompanied by a cold front at the surface. Peaks of sunshine during the late morning and early afternoon allowed the atmosphere to become unstable and develop severe thunderstorms as the frontal boundary trekked through the state. Large hail of up to 1.5 to 2 inches were observed in Mingo and Wayne Counties that afternoon as well as tree damage due to gusty winds in Cabell County.||Additional rain behind the frontal passage contributed to instances of flash flooding that evening in Kanawha and Wayne Counties. A swift water rescue was conducted near Alum Creek in Kanawha County as a nearby creek faced a deluge of water and rose onto the adjacent roadway.
